claim_scope: the conditional mean falls between two equally weighted valid scalar action modes
iterative mode refinement trades model evaluations for distance to a valid mode
an oracle straight-flow fixture reaches its assigned modes but does not represent learned flow-policy quality
candidate count and batch capacity change sequential forward count even when solver steps are fixed
data-mode validity remains distinct from independent scene-safety acceptance and deterministic fallback
equal validity and mode coverage can hide a mismatch between generated and target mode frequencies
best-of-N availability gains require a candidate-dependence assumption even when per-candidate acceptance probability is held fixed

code.config: standard-library v4 bimodal action, frequency-calibration, candidate-dependence, batching-budget, and candidate-gate fixture

data.name: procedural symmetric two-mode scalar action fixture

limitations: one-dimensional symmetric action modes with hand-selected base samples
mode-refinement update is not a DDPM or learned denoiser
straight flow uses oracle target assignment and cannot compare learned policy quality
ten authored samples and a known equal target distribution do not estimate population calibration or uncertainty
the twenty-percent marginal probability and iid/perfect-correlation structures are authored analytic endpoints, not measured candidate statistics
abstract forward budget does not measure batch-dependent wall-clock latency or memory
hand-authored blocked interval and fallback are not a collision checker or safety policy
